scope: second #1039 candidate on the rebuilt v2 editor route: the two carried pre-flip capability gaps (the v2 Send-to-Controller result never released; a stored v2 row that could not be renamed, duplicated or trashed, and whose rail organization the Shows Trash pruned), the three carried operator-plumbing correctives on the section 10 row-conversion command, and that runbook re-rehearsed on local D1 with rollback. The coordinated application activation is not delivered; see residualGaps.
invariants: The Shows rail is one list of personal Shows: rename, duplicate and Empty Trash act on a stored v2 row exactly as they act on a v1 record.
The persisted rail organization is keyed by Show id across both stored versions, so every reconciliation is against both collections; reconciling against one prunes the other's rows.
Every accepted v2 replacement updates the list row it describes, and a rolled-back save restores the durable name with the durable record.
Renaming a listed v2 row that is not open replaces it in place and never makes it the route's working copy; renaming an open one goes through its own history and save queue.

A successful Controller push result is released on the v2 route as it is on the v1 route, because the action row gates Run and Save while one stands; a failure waits for its notice and another artifact's result is untouched.
One delete by id serves both stored versions, and the row, its working copy, its history and any save failure are forgotten together.
The row-conversion command interrupts only after an outcome is durably recorded, so the count the operator asked for equals the count the store settled and the resume skips exactly those rows.
Migration qualification compiles a record at the Stage dimension the record's own Stage map gives it, resolved against the built-in maps and then the owner's, never an assumed 2D.
The operator entry point runs the command as shipped: it resolves the built-in Pattern catalogue, so it runs under the module runner rather than plain tsx.
Conversion never writes over a changed original; an already-v2 row is an idempotent no-op; a refused row stays recoverable and reported; rollback restores exactly the named identities.
The committed report carries identities, hashes, versions, statuses and bounded detail only - no Show name, Pattern source, Library source or record content.
